From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Beth Anytown <beth.anytown@cardinalhealth.com>, Cardinal Health Implementation <ops@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cardinal Health: acceptance threshold & load test coordination

Hi Beth / Ops team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — good energy on the integration. We want to lock the acceptance thresholds and the pragmatic load test plan so your SREs can start running the smoke tests next week. To make the handoff smooth I put together a short matrix below and attached a CSV you can edit with exact traffic mixes.

High-level asks:
- Confirm target p99 latency under baseline load (expected target: <= 280ms for 512-token average prompt)
- Confirm throughput target (concurrent sessions and sustained qps) — I filled a suggestion column in the attached matrix
- Share a list of endpoints and sample prompt traces you want included in the run (we'll seed KV cache accordingly)

Suggested acceptance matrix (editable in attached CSV):
- Baseline (20 concurrent, 50 qps sustained) -> p50/p95/p99 tokens
- Peak burst (120 concurrent, 350 qps for 5m) -> observe tail latency and error rate
- Cold-start measurement (first-request latency after 30m idle)
- Stability run (6h at 80% expected sustained QPS) -> error rate < 0.5%

I've CC'd Monica (CS) and Karthik (inference eng) for operational details. Monica — can you take the lead on scheduling a 60-min run with their SRE and map the test windows? Karthik — after Beth confirms the matrix we'll stage a short run and share telemetry.

Attachments: cardinal_test_matrix_v1.csv (CSV)

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. I attached a filled version of your CSV with our proposed traffic splits and preferred test windows (attached as cardinal_test_matrix_v1.csv). A few clarifications from our side:

- Our initial acceptance gate is p99 <= 300ms on 90% of API calls for the primary inference endpoint (we can tolerate short fanout spikes during peak hours but want strong tail SLAs)
- Sustained throughput target for stage is 220 qps (we'll run ramp tests to validate autoscaling behavior)
- For stability runs we prefer an 8-hour window overnight (US Central) to avoid user impact
- We will provide sample prompt traces by EOD Wednesday; ops@cardinalhealth.com will be primary contact for the run day.

Attachment: cardinal_test_matrix_v1.csv (updated by Cardinal)

On scheduling — Tuesday/Wednesday next week are ideal for our SREs; please propose a window.

Best,
Beth Anytown
Integration Lead, Cardinal Health
beth.anytown@cardinalhealth.com | +1 312-555-0222

Quick internal note and plan:

Thanks Beth for the updates — the Cardinal-updated matrix looks good. Proposed immediate next steps from CS:
1) Confirm test window: Wed 2026-10-14 02:00 - 10:00 UTC (Cardinal ops preferred overnight US Central)
2) Pre-run checklist (to be completed 48h before run):
   - Cardinal to upload sample prompt traces to the Drive link (see thread links)
   - Redwood to provision a dedicated test token with limited scope and TTL 24h before run
   - Karthik to share exact runner config and container image tags so ops can mirror locally
3) Acceptance criteria we will sign off on after the stability run:
   - p99 <= 300ms for primary endpoint on 95% of requests during baseline windows
   - sustained error rate < 0.5% over 8-hour stability run
   - no resource OOMs or degraded scheduling events in Redwood telemetry (we will share the trace IDs)

Karthik — can you confirm the runner config below and whether we should include a KV-cache warm-up step (we recommend a 10-minute warm-up at 30% QPS before baseline):
- container image: rw-infer/runner:20261004-rc
- concurrency model: adaptive batching, 128-token bucket, max batch size 64
- worker count: 8 (g4dn-equivalent nodes)

I will propose the calendar invite once we have Karthik's confirmation and Beth's final OK for 10/14. Ben — looping you to ensure legal/procurement is aware of the temporary test token and any egress constraints.

Monica Patel

Subject: Re: Cardinal Health: acceptance threshold & load test coordination

Confirming runner config and early telemetry from a short validation run we kicked off in staging this morning. We mirrored Cardinal's traffic mix from the CSV and ran a 30-minute stability probe at 75% of target QPS. Summary below and attached pdf with charts.

Staging validation highlights:
- Config: rw-infer/runner:20261004-rc, 8 workers, adaptive batching, max batch 64
- Warm-up: 10 minutes at 30% QPS applied (recommended)
- 30-min probe at 165 QPS (75% of cardinal's 220 qps target):
   - p50 = 42ms, p95 = 86ms, p99 = 182ms for 512-token median prompts
   - sustained error rate = 0.08% (mostly transient 429s during a single burst)
   - memory/CPU: within expected envelope; no OOMs or throttling events flagged in telemetry

Next steps / requests:
- We recommend Cardinal run the full 8-hour stability window on 2026-10-14 as discussed.
- We'll provision the dedicated test token and a recovery playbook (token revoke + fallback routing) 24h before run.
- Attachment: latency_summary_20261005.pdf contains charts + sample traces and the exact trace IDs for Redwood logs.

I can join the run day for live triage; propose we add an on-call rotation in the calendar invite (Monica to set).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
